https://www.dw.com/en/russian-gru-spies-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MVCs Bomb experts were able to disarm an explosives-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport in a failed attack now definitively attributed to Russia's GRU military intelligence agency Image: Axel Schmidt/REUTERS Advertisement Germany's Welt am Sonntag (WaS) newspaper has cited intelligence reports tying the recent failed drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport directly to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency . In an article published on Saturday, Welt am Sonntag said that a man with known ties to the GRU was responsible for operational logistics in the attempted attack. Further, it said those ties were known to German authorities when the man entered the country from Turkey, nevertheless, he was not surveilled after arrival. Classified security assessments cited by the paper say the Russian national is now in his home country after departing to Serbia on a flight from Berlin-Brandenburg Airport. A second man, a Belarus citizen, was also cited as an accomplice in the report. Germany blames Russia for attempted terror attack in Leipzig To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Explosives thought to have entered Germany from Bulgaria and Serbia German intelligence sources said that the explosives used in the incident were likely smuggled into Germany via truck from Bulgaria and Serbia and then stored in underground depots once they arrived in Leipzig. Berlin quickly made clear that forensic evidence found at Leipzig/Halle Airport — including drone configuration, explosives and trigger mechanisms used in other Russian hybrid attacks — pointed to a Russian plot. In early August, German tabloid BILD reported that authorities had found DNA traces on the drone's remote control antenna. Those samples were said to have matched DNA found at the scene of a July 20, 2024, arson attack at a Leipzig logistics facility operated by German courier company DHL. Leipzig attack averted but Russian escalation will continue The incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport — a hub for military aid destined for Ukraine — occurred on the evening of August 4 and involved an explosives-laden drone that was found near a Ukrainian transport jet. Authorities were able to disarm the drone and after public speculation that Moscow was behind the incident the German government officially blamed Russia in early September . Saturday's article said Berlin made the attribution on the basis of the intelligence reports cited. In response to its conclusion, Germany announced the closure of the Russian Consulate General in Bonn. The Kremlin in turn reacted by closing Goethe Institutes — a German cultural exchange outfit — across Russia. As in numerous similar hybrid attacks prior, Russia has denied any involvement in the incident. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Toledo police investigate a shooting at the Old West End festival in Toledo, Ohio, on 6 June 2026. Photograph: Rebecca Benson/The Blade/AP View image in fullscreen Toledo police investigate a shooting at the Old West End festival in Toledo, Ohio, on 6 June 2026. Photograph: Rebecca Benson/The Blade/AP Ohio Charges dropped against man arrested in mass shooting at Ohio festival that wounded 12 Eljay Crisp-Carr, 20, spent five months behind bars before prosecutors asked to dismiss charges Marina Dunbar Fri 30 Oct 2026 13.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ohio prosecutors on Friday dropped charges against a man arrested in connection with the 6 June shooting at Toledo’s Old West End festival that injured 12 people. Eljay Crisp-Carr, 20, had faced more than 50 felony charges stemming from the shooting, including 25 counts of attempted murder. He was released after spending about five months behind bars. But during a hearing Friday before the judge Lori Olender of the Lucas county court of common pleas, prosecutors requested that the charges against Crisp-Carr be dismissed. His mother, April Carr, told news outlet WKYC she was “ecstatic” about the outcome. “I’m beyond excited because what mother wants their child to be broadcast across the world for something they didn’t do?” she said. Crisp-Carr’s defense team believes another person involved in the shooting remains at large. “Now we’re still concerned that there is still somebody out here who actually did do the shooting, and as far as we’re concerned, that guy might be still out here still shooting,” defense attorney Alex Bodiford told WKYC. The local news outlet WTVG reported that attorneys for Crisp-Carr had said he was not even at the festival when the shooting occurred. Lawyers for Crisp-Carr said they had video and cellphone evidence that supported his alibi, according to WTVG. The Lucas county prosecutor’s office issued a statement to the media Friday morning explaining its decision, noting the dismissal was without prejudice – meaning charges can be refiled if necessary – though also acknowledging that it had found evidence apparently supporting Crisp-Carr’s defense. “Due to new and developing evidence, the state of Ohio asked the court to dismiss the charges against Eljay Crisp-Carr without prejudice, and the court granted the request,” the prosecutor’s office said. “In September 2026, the Lucas county prosecutor’s office informed Mr Crisp-Carr’s attorney of discovery that may support his defense.” The statement also addressed the status of the investigation, saying it was ongoing. “The Toledo Police Department continues its investigation,” the statement said. “Both the department and our office remain committed to following the evidence and getting it right, just as we are in every case. As we said after the shooting in June, we will try this case in a courtroom, not in a court of public opinion.” Speaking with WTVG after the charges against him were dropped, Crisp-Carr said: “God is good.” He maintained that he had always known he was innocent and believed authorities had mistaken him for someone else. When asked whether he believed the mistaken identification came from photographs, Crisp-Carr responded: “Yes, sir. Just picking with me.” He also said he had attempted to explain to authorities that he was not the individual shown in the photograph. “They told me I was a monster,” Crisp-Carr said. “They just incriminated me.” The Old West End festival mass shooting erupted when a fight between rival groups apparently escalated into two people shooting at each other, although they were not among the wounded. Hundreds of people were attending the annual festival in a historic district of Toledo, a city on the western edge of Lake Erie. Organizers canceled the event’s second day because of the shooting. As of Friday, there had been more than 385 mass shootings in the US so far for the year, according to the Gun Violence Archive , a nonpartisan resource which defines such cases as those in which four or more victims are wounded or killed. The US perennially has had high rates of mass shootings, prompting many to call on the federal government to implement more substantial gun control. But Congress has not implemented such measures.
